title: go/no-go verdict for the 24 GB and 16 GB VRAM classes
question: docs/29 F3 asks for a 24 GB profile and a 16 GB profile. docs/34 did the arithmetic. This receipt turns that arithmetic into a decision, re-derived on the constants the physical RTX 5090 qualification actually measured, and states go or no-go for each class.
claim_scope: NO 24 GB OR 16 GB BOARD HAS EVER BEEN STARTED IN THIS PROJECT. Every per-class figure in this receipt is arithmetic over inputs measured on 32 GB-class hardware, and every such figure is labelled prediction with the formula that produced it. Nothing here is a fit claim. No 16 GB profile has been measured for memory, context, throughput or fidelity, and no width below 4 bits has ever been measured for fidelity in this model family at all.

labelling_convention.measured: read out of an engine log or nvidia-smi on named hardware in a named receipt; the receipt is cited on the same line
labelling_convention.prediction: computed here; carries `formula`, and its inputs are themselves either measured or predictions
labelling_convention.external_unverified: a third-party report we did not run and cannot reproduce; never mixed into an arithmetic chain
labelling_convention.size_terminology: serialized bytes are what a checkpoint occupies on disk; resident weight bytes are what the loader keeps on the device; activation, CUDA-graph and KV are separate quantities. None of them is called VRAM, and the KV figure is never folded into the weight figure.

physical_5090_qualification.why_not_0_97: 0.97 x 31.4 GiB = 30.45 GiB starts and serves text but cannot serve the combined 236,824-token plus 7 MP request: vLLM spends every byte freed by a lower weight or activation figure on KV instead (272,570 -> 280,017 tokens at 0.97 with expandable_segments) and still OOMs with 26.5 MiB free. Lowering max_pixels is strictly worse. This is the single most consequential input to every class prediction below, and it moves the utilisation constant used throughout from 0.97 to 0.955.

usable_fraction_0_98125.basis: measured: 31.4 GiB on a 32 GB board (31.4/32), read out of the physical 5090's own startup line 'Free memory on device (30.9/31.4 GiB) on startup'
usable_fraction_0_98125.what_the_numerator_is: cudaMemGetInfo TOTAL, i.e. board framebuffer total minus the driver reserve - NOT free memory, and not the nvidia-smi FB Total either. On this card nvidia-smi reports FB Total 32,607 MiB and FB Reserved 458 MiB, so cudaMemGetInfo total = 32,149 MiB = 31.3955 GiB = 33,710,669,824 B, which is the 31.4 the engine prints. It coincides with the idle-free figure only because idle used was 2 MiB.
usable_fraction_0_98125.mechanism_verified_in_source: vllm/v1/worker/utils.py request_memory(): 'requested_memory = math.ceil(init_snapshot.total_memory * cache_config.gpu_memory_utilization)', then 'if init_snapshot.free_memory < requested_memory: raise'. The log line is that error's format string, 'Free memory on device (free/total GiB) on startup', so its second number is total_memory, not a usable-after-free figure. MemorySnapshot fills both from one call: vllm/utils/mem_utils.py line 146, 'self.free_memory, self.total_memory = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(device)'. Read out of the pinned r34 image on disk at /var/tmp/gg-rootfs/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/, i.e. the same image the qualification ran, not from upstream master.
usable_fraction_0_98125.arithmetic_that_confirms_it: ceil(31.3955 x 0.955) = 29.98 GiB, the budget the engine logged, and 29.98 / 0.955 = 31.3927 GiB recovers total to within 3 MiB. A second log arm makes it exact rather than coincidental: at utilisation 0.7643 the engine printed a 24.0 GiB budget with free = 30.9, and its two --kv-cache-memory-bytes hints (3,385,755,786 to fit the request, 10,799,671,296 to fill the card) differ by 6.9047 GiB = free - requested, putting requested at 23.9953 = ceil(31.3955 x 0.7643). Budget therefore tracks TOTAL; free only gates whether startup is allowed.
usable_fraction_0_98125.correction_history: an earlier revision of this receipt asserted the numerator was free-at-idle and warned TwentyFourGigProxy against a double-count that does not exist. That was wrong, it is corrected here, and the value 0.98125 is unaffected. Credit: TwentyFourGigProxy, who read the source and produced the 0.7643 log arm.
usable_fraction_0_98125.rounding_note: the exact fraction is 31.3955/32 = 0.98111; 0.98125 is used because 31.4 is what the engine printed. The difference is 0.003 GiB at 24 GiB and 0.002 at 16 GiB, below every other tolerance in this receipt.
usable_fraction_0_98125.supersedes: docs/34 §3 used 0.98094 from an external note (31.39/32). The difference is 0.01 GiB at 24 GB and 0.005 GiB at 16 GB, i.e. immaterial, but the measured value is now the one on the record.
usable_fraction_0_98125.how_to_transfer_it_to_another_board: do NOT scale the driver reserve with board size. The right procedure is to read that board's own nvidia-smi FB Total and FB Reserved and use total-minus-reserved, because the reserve depends on the board, the driver, ECC state and whether a display is attached. For a 24 GB board the scaled constant and the fixed-reserve model happen to agree: 24 x 0.98125 = 23.550 against 24,576 - 458 = 24,118 MiB = 23.5527 GiB, and against a 4090-style FB Total of 24,564 MiB it gives 23.541 GiB. All three are within 0.012 GiB, so the 24 GB class numbers in this receipt stand under either model - but that agreement is a coincidence of this reserve size, not a law.
usable_fraction_0_98125.still_one_board: the reserve is measured on one board. TwentyFourGigProxy's ballasted proxy arm will report the printed total on an effectively smaller card; if a different board or driver reserves materially more, this constant needs restating per board rather than renumbering.

utilisation_0_955.basis: measured: the value at which all seven gates pass on the physical card. 0.97 is NOT usable for a multimodal profile - it serves text and fails the combined long-text plus 7 MP request.
utilisation_0_955.supersedes: docs/34 §3 and §5.3 used 0.97, which is why the 24 GB length published there (40,960 with MTP-3) is retired by this receipt. This is the single largest correction the physical qualification forces on the class arithmetic.
utilisation_0_955.generality_caveat: the mechanism that makes 0.97 unsafe is engine behaviour, not board size: vLLM spends every freed byte on KV, so a higher utilisation does not leave transient vision allocations anywhere to live. It therefore transfers to smaller boards, where the absolute slack is smaller still. Assuming 0.97 on a 24 GB or 16 GB board would be assuming the opposite of what we measured.

non_kv_overheads_2_50.basis: measured on the physical 5090 at the qualified config, receipts/qualification-5090-context.json -> gates[*].measured_engine_usage_gib. The rental figures were 1.78/0.28/0.46 = 2.52.
non_kv_overheads_2_50.conservatism: carrying a 32 GB activation figure to a 16 GB card is deliberately conservative: activation profiling scales with the permitted image and the batched-token count, both of which a smaller profile lowers. It is still a carried number, not a measured one for those classes.

self_validation_on_the_only_measured_boa.meaning: the two-step card model reproduces the one engine budget we have ever seen logged to 0.01 GiB. That is the strongest available evidence for the model, and it is evidence from exactly one board.

32_gib.label: free_at_startup measured; the rest prediction, validated above against the logged 29.98

card_budget_model.softest_numbers: 0.98125 and 0.955 are still one board's constants. A board that reserves more for a display output, or a driver with a different allocator, moves both. This is why each class verdict below ends in a startup requirement rather than a number.

how_the_engine_actually_sizes_this.source: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py in the pinned r34 image. get_kv_cache_capacity() returns int(max_concurrency * max_model_len) and that is what the log line 'GPU KV cache size: N tokens' prints (the comment above it says so: 'GPU KV cache size in tokens = max_concurrency * max_model_len'). get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config() computes max_concurrency = num_blocks / cdiv(max_memory_usage_per_request, memory_per_block).
how_the_engine_actually_sizes_this.consequence: the reported token count is NOT pool_bytes / per_token_cost. It is a per-request quantity scaled by the window. For a hybrid model each request carries a FIXED cost (draft KV under MTP, recurrent-state pages, page padding) in addition to a per-token cost, so the correct law is affine in the window, and the apparent per-token rate falls as the window grows.
how_the_engine_actually_sizes_this.corroborating_detail: the two reported token counts, 265,122 and 62,557, are not multiples of the 1,600-token attention block size (265,122/1600 = 165.70, and 62,557 is odd), which rules out num_blocks x block_size and confirms the concurrency route. Credit: TwentyFourGigProxy spotted this.
how_the_engine_actually_sizes_this.why_this_matters_here: the previous form used in this receipt, KV_bytes = H + c_tok*T with H = 0.20 GiB, under-charges short windows, which is exactly the failure mode docs/34 §4 named when it chose to hold a fixed term outside the per-token rate - it just sized that term far too small.

formulas.tensor_floor: per_token_floor = 2 (K and V) * 4 kv heads * 256 head_dim * 1 byte (fp8) * 16 full_attention layers = 32,768 B/token
formulas.pool_needed_for_one_request: P(L) = a * L + M, with a the true per-token cost and M the fixed per-request cost, both per KV-configuration (MTP-3 and MTP-off differ)
formulas.what_the_engine_reports: T_reported = int((P / (a*L + M)) * L), i.e. concurrency x window; so P = a*T + M*(T/L), which is how a and M are recovered from a logged (P, T, L) triple
formulas.publishable: the largest multiple of 4,096 that leaves >= 15 % headroom, i.e. L such that a*L + M <= KV_avail/1.15. Retained for continuity with docs/34 §5.3, though with a mechanistic law it is now partly a double-count.

kv_model.why_only_16_layers: KV exists only on the 16 full_attention layers; the 48 GDN layers keep a fixed-size recurrent state per sequence instead of a per-token cache. That asymmetry is the entire reason a 27 B model can hold 262,144 tokens on a 32 GB card.

mtp3_fp8_parameters.status: MEASURED. Four startup refusals on one physical RTX 5090, two windows per KV configuration, max_num_seqs 1, fp8 KV, same image and revision: receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json (sha256 d336df53786f1b0aa7efa63a527871f19b7e80c10e0b6e3e2375ce78d38eb4c1), measured by TwentyFourGigProxy.
mtp3_fp8_parameters.solve: a3 = (9.13 - 4.88) GiB / (262,144 - 131,072) = 34,816.0 B/token EXACTLY, which is 32,768 x 17/16 - the fp8 tensor floor plus exactly one padding sixteenth. M3 = 4.88 GiB - 131,072 x 34,816 = 0.6300 GiB.
mtp3_fp8_parameters.independent_self_check: inverting the law reproduces the engine's own printed 'estimated maximum model length' figures: 81,600 tokens needs 0.63 + 81,600 x 34,816 / 2^30 = 3.2759 GiB against a pool printed as 3.27, and the MTP-off law puts 128,576 at 4.0834 against 4.08 printed.
mtp3_fp8_parameters.how_it_relates_to_the_bounds_this_receip: the a3 range [32,768, 34,816] contained the truth and resolved to its UPPER endpoint, which retrospectively validates reading the engine's 'may waste at most 6.25%' line as a per-token ceiling. The M3 range [0.676, 1.176] did NOT contain 0.63, and the reason is a real methodological flaw worth recording: I inverted an ALLOCATED pool (9.28 GiB available at L = 262,144) whereas the law needs the pool a window REQUIRES (9.13 GiB). Because max_concurrency = num_blocks / cdiv(...) involves flooring and a ceiling, reported concurrency is not exactly pool / requirement, so inverting an allocation over-estimates the fixed term. Measuring the refusal threshold at two windows, as the run above did, reads the requirement directly and is strictly the better method.
mtp3_fp8_parameters.what_this_retires: the 36,773.9 B/token single rate this receipt first used, and the 0.20 GiB H reserve behind it. That rate implied 36,765 B/token against a measured 34,816, i.e. it was above even the engine's padding ceiling.

mtp_off_fp8_parameters.agreement_with_docs_34: docs/34 §4's 32,929.0 B/token is within 0.009 % of the measured per-token cost. That section's rate was right; what was wrong was treating it as the whole cost.
mtp_off_fp8_parameters.correction_to_this_receipt: I had bounded M0 at 'at most 0.039 GiB, and 0.000 at the top of the range'. Measured it is 0.14 GiB, which is ABOVE my bound - the same allocated-versus-required inversion error, in the same direction. This lowers the MTP-off rows slightly relative to my previous revision.
mtp_off_fp8_parameters.what_it_confirms: the fixed per-request term is overwhelmingly MTP's: 0.63 GiB with MTP-3 against 0.14 GiB without, a 0.49 GiB difference per request. docs/34 §4 reasoned that the residual over the tensor floor was MTP-driven rather than GDN-driven, and that is now measured rather than argued.

mtp_3_true_total_cost.detail: MTP-3 costs 0.252 GiB of draft weights PLUS the entire 0.45 GiB CUDA-graph pool, which the same run measured at 0.00 GiB with MTP off, so non-KV overheads are 2.50 GiB with MTP-3 and 2.05 GiB without. On top of that it adds 0.49 GiB of fixed KV per request. On a 24 GB board that is about 35 % of the whole KV pool, which is the structural reason the 16 GB MTP-3 row is not short but absent.

retired_H_reserve.status: RETIRED and now superseded by measured values: the fixed per-request term is 0.63 GiB under MTP-3 and 0.14 GiB without.
retired_H_reserve.why_it_was_wrong: the shape was right - the engine's capacity formula does carry a fixed per-request term - but 0.20 GiB was three times too small for MTP-3 and slightly too large for MTP-off, so the old model was simultaneously too generous where it mattered most and too harsh elsewhere.

kv_4bit.label: prediction, never measured
kv_4bit.status: the pinned r34 build accepts int4_per_token_head, turboquant_4bit_nc and turboquant_k3v4_nc among others, but every published number here used fp8, and the fidelity protocol resolves the KV cache to bfloat16 (receipts/kld5-10M-*.json -> reference_identity), so it cannot see KV error even for the profiles that already ship fp8. No 4-bit-KV context length may be published by either class until that dtype has been swept.

class_24_gib.headline: at 24 GB no new checkpoint is required. The already-published context edition fits with measured resident weights, and the only thing that changes is the window.
class_24_gib.artifact: malaiwah/Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-K5K6-context, unchanged, served with the int8 input overlay

fidelity.label: measured, and it transfers unchanged because it is the same weights. A 24 GB profile carries no new fidelity risk of any kind.

resident_weights_gib.label: measured
resident_weights_gib.choice: the verdict uses 18.41, the larger of the two measured figures

kv_budget_gib.label: prediction
kv_budget_gib.comparison: the same checkpoint had 9.28 GiB of KV measured on a 32 GB board. A 24 GB board leaves about one sixth of that, and that single ratio is the whole story of the class.

class_24_gib.read_this_before_using_any_length_below: the KV cost parameters behind these lengths are now MEASURED (kv_model.mtp3_fp8_parameters, mtp_off_fp8_parameters), so the windows are point predictions rather than ranges. What is still a prediction is the CARD: no physical 24 GB board has been started. The MTP-3 figure this receipt first published, 32,768, is retired at the conservative resident measurement and confirmed reachable at the optimistic one - which is why the class is published at 24,576.

mtp_3_fp8.label: prediction from measured KV parameters
mtp_3_fp8.the_rule_is_on_MEMORY: docs/34 §5.3 defines the >= 15 % rule as 'the largest multiple of 4,096 whose REQUIREMENT leaves >= 15 % headroom against KV_avail', i.e. a*L + M <= pool/1.15, so L <= (pool/1.15 - M)/a. An earlier revision of this receipt applied it as L <= L_max/1.15, the token form, which is equivalent only when M = 0 - exactly the assumption the refusal measurements retired. Every length below uses the memory form. Credit: TwentyFourGigPublish caught it.

at_the_pool_the_proxy_measured.basis: 18.19 GiB resident, the figure this card loads at

at_the_conservative_resident.basis: 18.41 GiB resident, the larger of our two measurements

mtp_3_fp8.why_24576_is_the_published_figure: it clears the >= 15 % memory rule at the pool the proxy actually measured, and it still FITS at the conservative resident figure with a 10.7 % margin. 20,480 is what the rule alone would give at the conservative pool; 24,576 is what docs/34 publishes and what the proxy converged on independently, and the gap between the two is exactly the difference between our two measured resident-weight figures. A board that loads at 18.41 GiB should serve 20,480 if it wants the full rule margin.

32768.note: started and gated on the proxy at the 1.79 GiB pool, but below the rule margin there and infeasible at the conservative resident, so it is not a publishable default

mtp_off_fp8.status_of_that_number: STARTED AND GATED, not merely computed: the ballasted 24 GiB proxy arm ran this window and passed 7/7 gates with a measured 2.60 GiB pool, 76,032 allocated tokens, 1.69x concurrency and 70.8 % headroom (receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json). It is published BECAUSE it was started, in preference to the larger windows the arithmetic allows.

what_the_15pct_rule_would_allow.label: prediction
what_the_15pct_rule_would_allow.formula: memory form: a*L + M <= pool/1.15, so L <= (pool/1.15 - M)/a, rounded down to a 4,096 multiple; pools 2.6002 and 2.382 GiB give 69,157 and 62,970 -> 65,536 and 61,440
what_the_15pct_rule_would_allow.correction: an earlier revision printed 69,632 here from the token form L_max/1.15; 69,632 needs 2.2756 GiB against a 2.2610 GiB cap and FAILS the rule. At the conservative pool both forms happen to give 61,440, which is why the error was invisible there.

57344.status: inside the envelope and never started; named as arithmetically available, not published

mtp_off_fp8.overheads_detail: MTP off measures peak_activation 1.68 (0.10 lower than MTP-3's 1.78 - that delta is the draft model's activation), non_torch 0.27 and a CUDA-graph pool of 0.00, so 1.95 GiB against 2.50 with MTP-3. Sanity: 22.49 - 1.95 - 17.94 measured MTP-off resident = 2.60 GiB, the board arm's measured pool to the hundredth.
mtp_off_fp8.history_of_this_row: 45,056 in this receipt's first revision (right number, wrong reasons: a 0.20 GiB reserve and no CUDA-graph credit), then 49,152, then 57,344 as the corrections landed - and back to 45,056 because that is the window that was actually started. The arithmetic journey is recorded because the intermediate numbers were published; the published value now rests on a gate pass rather than on a model.
mtp_off_fp8.why_not_publish_the_larger_number: publishing an unstarted 57,344 or 61,440 while holding a gate-passing 45,056 would invert this receipt's own rule that 'predicted' and 'allocated' are different sentences. The headroom is stated above so nothing is hidden; the proxy receipt's prediction_2.note declines to raise it for the same reason.

sensitivity_to_the_two_resident_measurem.why_24576_and_not_28672_or_32768: 24,576 is the only 4,096-multiple robust across BOTH of our measured resident figures. 28,672 falls to a 1.3 % margin at the conservative one and 32,768 fails it outright, even though the proxy arm started and gated 32,768 on a card that loads at 18.19 GiB.
sensitivity_to_the_two_resident_measurem.measured_outcome: the ballasted arm at a 22.49 GiB budget with the card held to 23.553 GiB free allocated 33,760 tokens for a 32,768 window (1.03x) and passed all seven gates. So 32,768 works on an 18.19 GiB-resident board and not on an 18.41 GiB one; 24,576 is independent of which a given board reproduces.
sensitivity_to_the_two_resident_measurem.label: pools and L_max values are predictions; allocations and gate results are measured in receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json

class_24_gib.what_go_means: go to publish this as a 24 GB serving profile of an existing artifact, with 24,576 labelled a prediction and 45,056 labelled started-on-a-proxy, and go to run the physical qualification. It does NOT mean a card may print a token count as a physical-board fact: 'predicted', 'allocated on a ballasted proxy' and 'allocated on a 24 GB board' are three different sentences and only the third closes the class.
class_24_gib.gate_before_any_fit_claim: one startup on a physical 24 GB board, nvidia-smi before and after, resident weights / activation / non-torch / graph / KV pool / allocated tokens read out of the engine log, needle retrieval at >= 0.98 x the published length, one combined long-text plus >= 7 MP image request, the 30-case vision suite against the measured 24/30, throughput warmed with sampler and reasoning effort printed, and a receipt with the field set of release-evidence-context.json.
class_24_gib.optional_and_not_required: M24-L (docs/34 §5) is a new lower-bitrate conversion. Under the measured KV law its 0.86 GiB of released resident weights would buy about 26,000 more MTP-3 tokens. It is optional, it carries new fidelity risk, and it is explicitly NOT part of this go: the class is served by an artifact that already exists and already has a measured KLD.

kv_capacity_law_was_wrong_twice_and_is_n.status: CLOSED. Mechanism read from the pinned engine's source; both parameter pairs measured by two-window startup refusals in receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json (sha256 d336df53786f1b0aa7efa63a527871f19b7e80c10e0b6e3e2375ce78d38eb4c1). Nothing about the KV law is now a range.
kv_capacity_law_was_wrong_twice_and_is_n.how_it_surfaced: TwentyFourGigProxy reported an apparent 56,642 B/token at a 32,768 window against 37,584 at native length, and noticed that neither reported token count is a multiple of the 1,600-token attention block - which cannot happen if the engine divides a pool by a per-token cost. Reading vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py showed why: capacity is reported as concurrency x window.
the_two_errors_and_their_causes: FORM: the first revision used H + c_tok*T with H = 0.20 GiB. The engine's law is affine in the window with a fixed per-request term. Consequence: short windows were under-charged, and the implied 36,765 B/token exceeded even the engine's own padding ceiling of 34,816 - so it was refutable from our own receipt alone.

METHOD: the second revision derived the parameters by inverting an ALLOCATED pool (9.28 GiB at L = 262,144) when the law needs the pool a window REQUIRES (9.13 GiB). Because max_concurrency divides by cdiv(...), reported concurrency is not exactly pool/requirement, so the inversion biased the fixed term high for MTP-3 (0.676-1.176 GiB against a measured 0.63) and low for MTP-off (<=0.039 GiB against a measured 0.14). Measuring the refusal threshold at two windows avoids the inversion entirely and is the method that should have been asked for first.

mtp_3.note: 34,816 = 32,768 x 17/16 exactly - the fp8 tensor floor plus one padding sixteenth

non_kv_overheads_gib.why_they_differ: MTP off drops the CUDA-graph pool (0.45 -> 0.00 GiB) and the draft model's activation (1.78 -> 1.68 GiB); non_torch is 0.27 in both

how_every_published_length_moved.24_gib_mtp_3: 32,768 (revision 1) -> 20,480 (revision 2, bounded) -> 24,576 MEASURED-PARAMETER FINAL. 32,768 needs 1.692 GiB: it fits the 1.80 GiB pool this card's 18.19 GiB resident leaves, and not the 1.58 GiB that the conservative 18.41 GiB figure leaves, so it is not a safe default.
how_every_published_length_moved.24_gib_mtp_off: 45,056 -> 49,152 -> 57,344 -> 45,056 FINAL, and the final value is published because it is the window the ballasted proxy arm actually STARTED and gated 7/7, not because it is the largest the arithmetic allows. The arithmetic allows 80,208 at the measured pool and 61,440-65,536 under the memory-form headroom rule; those are stated as predictions beside it rather than published.
how_every_published_length_moved.16_gib_mtp_3: 8,192 -> withdrawn -> WITHDRAWN, now on a measured margin: 0.63 GiB of fixed term against a 0.553 GiB pool, short by 0.077 GiB.
how_every_published_length_moved.16_gib_mtp_off: 12,288 -> 16,384 -> 28,672 -> 32,768 -> 28,672 FINAL, where the corrected MTP-off overheads and the corrected memory-form rule agree. Still 1.75x what docs/34 §6.2 predicted, with S16-V-long at 36,864. Unstarted, unlike the 24 GB row.
how_every_published_length_moved.reading: the corrections did not all point the same way. MTP-3 got more expensive and MTP-off got substantially cheaper, which is why the law had to be replaced rather than its constants nudged, and why the 16 GB design study is now more attractive than when it was written even though its verdict is unchanged.

kv_capacity_law_was_wrong_twice_and_is_n.what_survived_all_of_it: both class decisions, untouched. The 24 GB GO rests on measured weights (18.41 GiB against a 19.99 GiB budget) and the 16 GB NO-GO rests on absent fidelity (no sub-4-bit width in this family has ever been measured). Neither was ever a capacity argument. Every number that moved was a window.

no_physical_board_in_either_class.status: OPEN, and it is now the only capacity-side gap
no_physical_board_in_either_class.detail: the 24 GiB qualification is a PROXY: a 32 GB RTX 5090 with the engine budgeted to 22.49 GiB and the card ballasted to 23.553 GiB free. Its own receipt records physical_board_gate: open. No 24 GB or 16 GB board has been started.
no_physical_board_in_either_class.why_the_proxy_is_nevertheless_worth_some: the ballasted arm reproduces both the budget AND the outside-budget slack a real 24 GiB board would have, which is exactly the property the earlier rental proof lacked.

class_16_gib.verdict: NO-GO as a SKU. Publish as a design study.
class_16_gib.headline: every reachable 16 GB configuration requires at least one knob for which this project has no fidelity measurement of any kind, and the cheapest configuration that avoids all of them does not fit.

the_arithmetic_that_kills_the_safe_optio.configuration: the cheapest multimodal build that keeps the MLP stack at 4 bits: full_attention K3, linear_attention K3, MLP gate/up/down all K4, lm_head K3, MTP all K4, int8 embedding, BF16 vision tower

resident_gib.label: prediction
resident_gib.formula: byte law payload 13.235 GiB + 0.35 loader allowance

budget_gib.label: prediction
budget_gib.basis: docs/34 §3 at utilisation 0.97 and 2.52 GiB overheads

overshoot_gib.label: prediction
overshoot_gib.meaning: 0.88 GiB over budget BEFORE a single KV byte

overshoot_at_the_qualified_utilisation.label: prediction
overshoot_at_the_qualified_utilisation.formula: 13.58 - 12.49, where 12.49 uses the measured 0.955 utilisation and 2.50 GiB overheads
overshoot_at_the_qualified_utilisation.meaning: today's physical result makes the overshoot strictly worse, so the conclusion hardens rather than softens

the_arithmetic_that_kills_the_safe_optio.consequence: either the vision tower goes or the fourth MLP bit goes. The MLP stack is 17.113 B params, so one bit across gate+up+down is 1.992 GiB - the only lever large enough to matter at this size, and the worst measured buy per GiB in the whole knob ranking (docs/34 §7). A 16 GB multimodal build is therefore a SUB-4-BIT build by arithmetic, not by choice.

s16_v_candidate.status: candidate design. EVERY number in this object is a prediction. No 16 GB profile has been built, started, timed or scored.

bit_allocation.embed_tokens: BF16 on disk, int8 at load
bit_allocation.why_attention_gets_the_extra_bit: full_attention is the cheapest place to spend one, 0.1953 GiB per bit against 0.6445 for linear_attention, and it carries long-range retrieval

serialized_bytes.label: prediction
serialized_bytes.formula: byte law at the widths above, summed over roles, embedding at BF16 on disk

resident_payload_gib.label: prediction
resident_payload_gib.formula: same payload with the BF16 embedding replaced by its int8 resident form, 12,440,105,028 B / 2^30

mtp_off.label: prediction
mtp_off.formula: at the docs/34 §3 basis (utilisation 0.97, overheads 2.52, KV_avail 0.96 GiB), requirement 0.70 GiB, quoted as 37 % headroom

context_with_the_measured_kv_law.basis: utilisation 0.955; non-KV overheads 2.50 GiB with MTP-3 (1.78 activation + 0.27 non-torch + 0.45 CUDA-graph) and 1.95 GiB without (1.68 + 0.27 + 0.00 - MTP off drops both the CUDA-graph pool and the draft model's 0.10 GiB of activation); KV parameters as measured in kv_model. Budget 14.99 GiB. Both overhead figures are measured at the 8.4 MP cap on a 32 GB board; a 16 GB profile at 4.2 MP should measure its own activation, which would only help.

mtp_3.label: structural result from measured parameters
mtp_3.finding: MTP-3 IS IMPOSSIBLE AT 16 GB AT ANY WINDOW. The measured fixed per-request term is 0.63 GiB against a total pool of 0.553 GiB, so the request cannot be admitted before a single token is cached. The earlier 8,192 and 12,288 figures for this row are withdrawn, not reduced.
mtp_3.margin_of_the_impossibility: 0.077 GiB. It is close, which means a profile that shaved ~0.1 GiB of resident weights could reopen the question - but it would still be buying speculative decode with the whole of its context budget.
mtp_3.consequence: a 16 GB build is single-token-decode only, and loses the 56.48 % MTP acceptance and its throughput with it. The retired model hid this by charging MTP a flat 0.20 GiB.

mtp_off.label: prediction from measured KV parameters
mtp_off.correction: an earlier revision published 32,768 here from the token form L_max/1.15 = 32,917. 32,768 needs 1.1450 GiB against a rule cap of 1.1313, so it FAILS the rule - it fits the pool outright, but with 13.6 % margin rather than 15 %. The token form over-publishes by a full 4,096 step at this class precisely because the 0.14 GiB fixed term is a larger fraction of a small pool, which is what TwentyFourGigPublish predicted when it caught the error.
mtp_off.history_of_this_row: 12,288 (0.20 GiB reserve, no CUDA-graph credit) -> 16,384 (fixed term wrongly near zero) -> 28,672 (overheads 0.10 GiB high) -> 32,768 (token-form rule) -> 28,672, which is where the corrected overheads and the corrected rule form agree. Still 1.75x docs/34 §6.2's original figure.
mtp_off.unstarted: nothing at 16 GB has ever been started, so unlike the 24 GB MTP-off row this figure rests on arithmetic alone.

context_with_the_measured_kv_law.net_effect_on_the_16_gb_verdict: unchanged as a decision, and sharper as a design: without MTP the window is 28,672 rather than the 16,384 docs/34 §6.2 predicted, while MTP-3 is eliminated outright. The NO-GO does not move, because it rests on fidelity: no sub-4-bit width in this family has ever been measured. Capacity turned out not to be the obstacle it looked like, which makes this design study more attractive than when it was written, not less.

fidelity.label: UNKNOWN AND UNMEASURABLE FROM ANYTHING WE HAVE PUBLISHED
fidelity.nearest_measured_neighbour: K4, 0.010345 on shard 0 and 0.010604 over 10,480,640 positions, already the worst of the five published candidates with p99.9 0.5555 against the context build's 0.1642
fidelity.distance_from_that_neighbour: S16-V is one bit lower on each of gate/up/down, three lower on the linear-attention stack (online K6 -> K3), two lower on full attention (online K6 -> K4) and two lower on the head (K6 -> K4) - every one of them in the direction that made K4 the worst published candidate

extrapolation_range.label: prediction, extrapolation only
extrapolation_range.caveat: the measured ladder has NO point below 4 bits, so this is a range with a shape, not an estimate. A card that prints a fidelity number for any 16 GB profile without having run the suite is fabricating it.

resident_weights_gib.label: prediction
resident_weights_gib.formula: S16-V payload with full_attention K4 -> K3, releasing 0.1953 GiB

mtp_3.label: structural result from measured parameters
mtp_3.finding: also impossible in practice. KV_avail = 14.99 - 2.50 - 11.74 = 0.753 GiB against a measured fixed MTP-3 term of 0.63 GiB, which leaves 764 tokens under the memory-form rule and 3,793 even ignoring it - both below the 4,096 granularity this project publishes at. The extra bit does not buy speculative decode at this class.

mtp_off.label: prediction from measured KV parameters
mtp_off.formula: KV_avail = 14.99 - 1.95 - 11.542 = 1.502 GiB; engine ceiling L_max = (1.502 - 0.14) * 2^30 / 32,931.8 = 44,408; the memory-form rule allows L <= (1.502/1.15 - 0.14) * 2^30 / 32,931.8 = 38,020, so 36,864, needing 1.2706 GiB. Both rule forms agree on this row.

s16_v_long_variant.the_trade: the measured law changes what this bit is even for. It was framed as 'one bit on 16 of 64 layers against speculative decode at the advertised length'; with MTP-3 structurally impossible at 16 GB in both variants, the bit now buys context only - 36,864 against S16-V's 28,672 - and it is paid for with whatever K3 attention costs in retrieval, which is unmeasured. Neither variant may be published first.

class_16_gib.what_no_go_means: docs/34 §6 stays published as a design study: the byte budgets, the bit allocation and the acceptance gates are useful to anyone who wants to attempt this, and the error-driven allocator path (util/measure.py plus util/optimize.py over a byte budget) is the right way to build it. What may NOT happen is a released 16 GB artifact, a 16 GB row in any model card, a 16 GB context length quoted as a capability, or any fidelity number attached to a 16 GB profile.
conditions_that_would_flip_it_to_go: a measured KLD for at least one sub-4-bit width in THIS family on shard 0 of the v5 suite (512 contexts, 1,048,064 positions, the shared BF16 head), with the tail row and the exceedance counts, so the extrapolation range above is replaced by a number. This is the blocking condition, and it is cheap: it needs one conversion and one shard, no 16 GB card at all.

a startup on a physical 16 GB board with resident weights, activation, non-torch, graph and allocated KV tokens read out of the engine log, since the activation and CUDA-graph figures used here are carried from a 32 GB profile and have never been measured at a lower image cap
a needle-retrieval pass at the published length and a combined long-text plus image request at the 4.2 MP cap, because a K3 body has no measured retrieval behaviour
a non-termination / repetition check, weighted: two independent Q4 reports describe looping to context exhaustion, which mean KLD cannot see, and S16-V sits below Q4
class_16_gib.why_this_is_not_pessimism: the same arithmetic said yes at 24 GB with no new artifact at all. The 16 GB answer is different because the arithmetic itself forces a width nobody has measured, and because the one class of external evidence that exists for this model on 16 GB cards is negative.

external_unverified_reports.role: context for the 16 GB no-go. Not measurements of ours, never mixed into any arithmetic above, and not on the same axis as our resident-weight or KLD figures.

reports.claim: a ~12 GB IQ3_XXS-class GGUF of this model is unusable at long context on a 16 GB card
reports.verbatim: Useless on a 16GB RTX 5070 Ti with 64GB of RAM. ... Even with an IQ3_XXS quantization (~12GB), if you set the context size to 64K or 128K, you get less than 5 tok/s.
reports.source: r/LocalLLaMA megathread 1voojjz, u/GambAntonio, comment p3ui0np, created_utc 1786804153
reports.what_it_does_and_does_not_say: the reader's ~12 GB is his own parenthetical for the file, not a resident-weight measurement, and he states no KV dtype, engine version, utilisation or batch size. What survives that is the shape of the result: at a bitrate BELOW S16-V's, on a 16 GB card of the right generation, long context was reported unusable on throughput grounds - an axis this receipt's arithmetic cannot see at all, because every number here is a memory number.
reports.relevance_to_the_verdict: S16-V's measured-parameter window is 32,768 with MTP off, not 64K-128K, so it is not the same operating point; but a design whose window is a quarter of the one readers ask about, at a width nobody has scored, and which cannot run speculative decode at all, is not a SKU.

reports.claim: UD-Q4_K_XL on a 24 GB 4090 leaves about 18.4k usable context
reports.verbatim: I'm using unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL on a 4090. It loads fine but it only leaves me with about 18.4k context length on the vram, and it runs out after just a few prompts.
reports.source: r/LocalLLaMA megathread 1voojjz, u/arvzg, comment p3vfwqh, created_utc 1786813863
reports.artifact_size_on_our_axis: UD-Q4_K_XL is 17,923,394,624 B = 16.692 GiB serialized (docs/35, pinned artifacts) - serialized bytes, not resident weights, and not comparable with our 18.41 GiB resident figure
reports.relevance_to_the_verdict: an independent report that a ~16.7 GiB-serialized artifact on a 24 GB board lands near 18.4k tokens. When this receipt predicted 32,768 that looked like an unexplained outlier and I attributed it to fp8 KV, the 16-of-64-layer hybrid and single-sequence serving. With the KV law now measured, the comparable prediction is 24,576 with MTP-3 and a hard ceiling of 29,298 at the conservative resident figure, so this reader is no longer an outlier at all - he is roughly where the arithmetic now puts a 24 GB board. It remains a self-reported configuration with no KV dtype, engine version or utilisation, and llama.cpp's KV geometry is not ours, so it is corroboration of magnitude only.

24_gib.one_line: Ship a 24 GB serving profile of the already-published context edition and run the physical qualification: no conversion, no new fidelity risk, measured 0.003409 KLD carried unchanged. Window 24,576 with MTP-3 - the only 4,096-multiple robust across both of our measured resident figures - and 45,056 with MTP off, which a ballasted 24 GiB proxy started and gated 7/7 with 70.8 % headroom. Both rest on MEASURED KV parameters (a = 34,816 B/token with 0.63 GiB fixed under MTP-3; 32,931.8 with 0.14 GiB without). The remaining gap is the board itself: the 24 GiB evidence is a proxy on a 5090 and its own receipt records physical_board_gate: open.
24_gib.blocking_before_any_fit_claim: one startup on a physical 24 GB board

16_gib.one_line: Do not publish a 16 GB SKU. Publish docs/34 §6 as a design study. Every 16 GB path requires a sub-4-bit width, no sub-4-bit width in this family has ever been measured for KLD, we have no 16 GB card to measure on, and the only external evidence for this model at that class is a reader reporting a smaller quantization as unusable at long context.
16_gib.flip_condition: a measured sub-4-bit KLD on shard 0 plus a startup on a physical 16 GB board; the KLD half is cheap and unblocked and should be done first. Note that capacity is no longer the obstacle it looked like: with the KV law measured, S16-V reaches 28,672 tokens without MTP - it simply cannot run MTP-3 at all.

what_we_do_not_know: no sub-4-bit width of this architecture has ever been measured for fidelity, at any role, on any suite. Every 16 GB configuration needs at least one.
no 24 GB and no 16 GB board has ever been started here. The 24 GiB evidence is a ballasted proxy on a 32 GB RTX 5090 whose own receipt records physical_board_gate: open.
the two card constants, 0.98125 usable and 0.955 utilisation, come from one board, though the usable figure is now understood mechanically as cudaMemGetInfo total = FB total minus the driver reserve.

activation and non-torch figures are carried from a 32 GB profile; the CUDA-graph pool is now measured in both MTP modes (0.45 GiB with MTP-3, 0.00 without). A 16 GB profile at a 4.2 MP cap should still measure its own activation.

how the 0.63 GiB fixed per-request KV term splits between the GDN conv/SSM state, MTP draft KV and page padding. We know MTP dominates it - 0.63 with MTP-3 against 0.14 without - but no receipt of ours itemizes the pool.
the 4-bit KV dtypes are unmeasured and the current fidelity protocol resolves the KV cache to bfloat16, so it cannot measure them. No verdict here uses them.
throughput at these classes is entirely unknown. Every number in this receipt is a memory number, and the only negative external evidence we have for the 16 GB class is a throughput report.
retrieval behaviour at K3 attention is unknown, so the S16-V versus S16-V-long one-bit trade cannot be settled on paper.

nothing further about the KV law: a and M are measured in both MTP modes, and the 34,816 B/token figure is exactly 17/16 of the fp8 tensor floor, so the padding term is understood as well as measured.

open_work.item: measure a sub-4-bit width's KLD before committing to a 16 GB SKU
open_work.why_blocking: it is the only thing that converts the 0.03-0.10 extrapolation into a number, and it is the condition on which the 16 GB no-go flips
open_work.cost: one conversion plus shard 0 of the v5 suite; no 16 GB hardware required
open_work.gate: shard 0, 512 contexts, 1,048,064 positions, the shared BF16 head 25a30fd5f826da0abc4efc4cc71def9f02bcb8085f7175eee284d221dee4cfff, mean plus bootstrap interval plus the tail row and exceedance counts, paired against the published context build

open_work.item: obtain or emulate a 24 GB card for a real qualification rather than an engine-budget proof
open_work.why_blocking: the 24 GB go is a go to qualify, not a fit claim, and an emulated budget is not a hard-limit proof
open_work.lesson_from_today: the rental engine-budget proof at 30.24 GiB inside a 95.6 GiB card said utilisation 0.97 was fine. The physical RTX 5090 then failed the combined 236,824-token plus 7 MP request at exactly that utilisation, because vLLM spent every freed byte on KV and left the vision tower without the ~62 MiB of transient it needed, while lowering max_pixels made it strictly worse. An engine-budget proof carved out of a larger card keeps real headroom behind the budget, so it cannot see that failure mode.
open_work.the_objection_is_now_numeric_not_rhetori: the 24 GiB proxy ran both arms. Its budget-only arm - engine capped to 24.0 GiB on an otherwise free 32 GB card - peaked at 25,614 MiB during the image gates, which is 1,496 MiB MORE than the 24,118 MiB of CUDA-visible memory a 24 GiB board owns in total. It passed on bytes no such board has. The ballasted arm, which holds the card down to 23.553 GiB free as well as budgeting to 22.49 GiB, peaked at 24,050 MiB and passed by 68 MiB. That is the difference between a budget cap and a board, measured in megabytes (receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json).
open_work.what_remains: a physical 24 GB board. The proxy's own receipt records physical_board_gate: open, and the ballasted arm is the strongest available substitute rather than a replacement.
open_work.gate: the per-class gate listed under class_24_gib.gate_before_any_fit_claim

supersedes.docs/34 \u00a73: the class budget table is re-derived at the measured 0.98125 usable fraction, the measured 0.955 utilisation and the measured 2.50 GiB overheads. Weights+KV becomes 19.99 GiB at 24 GB (was 20.32) and 12.49 GiB at 16 GB (was 12.70).
supersedes.docs/34 \u00a75.3: the M24 published lengths become 24,576 with MTP-3 and 45,056 with MTP off. That replaces the 40,960/53,248 in that section and every intermediate revision of this receipt (32,768/45,056, then 20,480/49,152, then 24,576/57,344). 40,960 needs 2.06 GiB of KV against at most 1.80 GiB available; 45,056 is published because it was started and gated rather than because the arithmetic permits it, which it does with room to spare.
supersedes.docs/34 \u00a74: the per-token KV model H + c_tok*T is retired outright. The engine's capacity law is affine in the WINDOW - pool needed = a*L + M - and it reports concurrency x window, not pool / per-token cost. Measured: a = 34,816 B/token with a 0.63 GiB fixed term under MTP-3, and 32,931.8 with 0.14 GiB without. That section's 32,929.0 B/token was right to within 0.009 % as a per-token rate; what was wrong was treating it as the whole cost. The 0.20 GiB H reserve is gone.
supersedes.docs/34 \u00a75/\u00a76 non-KV overheads: 2.50 GiB (1.78 + 0.27 + 0.45) applies only with MTP-3. With MTP off the measured figures are 1.68 + 0.27 + 0.00 = 1.95 GiB, because the CUDA-graph pool goes to zero and the draft model's 0.10 GiB of activation goes with it. Sanity check on the measured board arm: 22.49 - 1.95 - 17.94 = 2.60 GiB, its measured MTP-off pool to the hundredth.
supersedes.docs/34 \u00a76.2: S16-V becomes 32,768 with MTP off - twice that section's 16,384 - and MTP-3 is withdrawn entirely, its 0.63 GiB fixed KV term exceeding the whole 0.553 GiB pool by 0.077 GiB. S16-V-long becomes 36,864 MTP-off and likewise cannot run MTP-3, reaching only 3,793 tokens. Both remain unstarted predictions for a design study.
supersedes.note: this receipt does not rewrite any published receipt. The earlier receipts remain valid for what they measured; this one is new evidence applied to the class arithmetic.

kv_law_and_24gib_proxy.what_it_supplies: the measured KV parameters in both MTP modes, the CUDA-graph pool in both modes, the ballasted-versus-budget-only peak comparison, and gate passes at both published lengths
kv_law_and_24gib_proxy.caveat: physical_board_gate: open - it is a ballasted proxy on a 32 GB RTX 5090

conventions.self_digest: content_sha256 is the sha256 of this document with generated_utc, generator, content_sha256 and content_sha256_excludes removed, canonicalised as json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) and encoded UTF-8 - the same recipe as receipts/collection-index.json, verified here by recomputing that file's digest plus cross-engine-comparator.json, capture-determinism.json and scored-window-offset.json and matching each stored value.
conventions.labels: every number is either measured with its receipt named on the same line, or carries an explicit prediction label with the formula that produced it. Preliminary third-party or in-flight results live in open_risks_to_this_verdict and external_unverified_reports and are never inputs to an arithmetic chain.

amendments.nature: additive: no pre-existing key or value in this file was altered, removed or renumbered by this amendment. It records why the 24 GB-class figures now in the body are what they are, so the decision is auditable separately from the values.

change_1_the_published_24_gb_mtp3_window.reason: at 32,768 the board-faithful proxy arm allocated 33,760 KV tokens for a 32,768 window - 1.03x concurrency and 5.8 % headroom against this project's own >= 15 % rule, which every other published length in docs/34 obeys. Worse, the figure fits or fails depending on which of our two resident-weight measurements applies: at 18.19 GiB resident the pool is 1.79-1.80 GiB and the engine supports ~35,774 tokens, but at the 18.41 GiB this receipt deliberately prefers the pool is 1.58 GiB and 32,768 does not fit at all. A published window may not sit between two of our own measurements of the same quantity.
change_1_the_published_24_gb_mtp3_window.why_24576: it needs 1.4269 GiB. At the measured 1.79 GiB pool that is 25.4 % headroom and it is the largest 4,096-multiple clearing the 15 % rule there; at the conservative 1.58 GiB pool it still fits, at 10.7 %. It is the only 4,096-multiple robust across BOTH measured resident figures - 28,672 collapses to 1.3 % at the conservative pool and 32,768 fails outright.
change_1_the_published_24_gb_mtp3_window.honest_limit: 24,576 clears the 15 % rule at the measured pool, not at the conservative one, where the rule alone would give 20,480. A board loading at 18.41 GiB should serve 20,480 if it wants the full margin. This is stated in docs/34 5.3.1 rather than buried.
change_1_the_published_24_gb_mtp3_window.recomputed_from: receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json kv_law_measured.law, not copied from any summary

change_2_the_24_gb_mtp_off_window.reason: the same recomputation does not contradict it. 45,056 needs 1.5219 GiB against the measured 2.60 GiB pool, 70.8 % headroom, and it survives the conservative resident figure at 56.5 %. It is also the window the proxy actually started and passed 7/7 gates at, allocating 76,032 tokens at 1.69x concurrency. The >= 15 % envelope reaches 65,536 and the engine ceiling is 80,208; both are named in the body as predictions and neither has been booted.

change_3_the_mtp_off_overhead_disagreeme.disagreement: SixteenGigVerdict derived the MTP-off rows from non-KV overheads of 2.05 GiB, which yields a published window of 57,344. TwentyFourGigPublish derived them from 1.95 GiB.
change_3_the_mtp_off_overhead_disagreeme.resolution: 1.95 GiB is correct. The disputed 0.10 GiB is the draft model's activation: receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json memory_component_comparison.table gives MTP-off peak_activation 1.68 against MTP-3's 1.78, with non_torch 0.27 and a CUDA-graph pool of 0.00, so 1.68 + 0.27 + 0.00 = 1.95.
change_3_the_mtp_off_overhead_disagreeme.the_arithmetic_that_settled_it: 22.49 - 1.95 - 17.94 (measured MTP-off resident) = 2.6002 GiB, which reproduces the board arm's independently measured 2.60 GiB MTP-off pool to the hundredth. The 2.05 figure gives 2.50 GiB and misses it by 0.10. A component estimate that cannot reproduce a measured pool is falsified by that pool.
change_3_the_mtp_off_overhead_disagreeme.accepted_by: SixteenGigVerdict, who verified it independently; and Main, who ruled that a started window is published in preference to a larger derived one, with the envelope and ceiling named beside it.

change_4_the_15_percent_rule_is_on_memor.what_was_wrong: an earlier revision applied the rule as L <= L_max/1.15, the token form. docs/34 5.3 defines it on memory: a*L + M <= pool/1.15, i.e. L <= (pool/1.15 - M)/a.
change_4_the_15_percent_rule_is_on_memor.why_it_matters_now: the two forms are equivalent only when M = 0, which is precisely the assumption the refusal measurements retired. With M > 0 the token form over-publishes.
change_4_the_15_percent_rule_is_on_memor.worked_case: at the measured 2.6002 GiB MTP-off pool the token form gives 69,632, which needs 2.2756 GiB against a 2.2610 GiB cap and FAILS the rule; the memory form gives 65,536, needing 2.1500 GiB for 20.9 %. At the conservative 2.382 GiB pool both forms give 61,440, which is why the error was invisible there.
change_4_the_15_percent_rule_is_on_memor.blast_radius: also corrected the 16 GB S16-V MTP-off row, 32,768 -> 28,672 (32,768 needs 1.1450 GiB against a 1.1313 GiB cap, 13.4 %). S16-V-long's 36,864 is unaffected; both forms agree there.

amendments.what_this_amendment_does_not_do: it does not close the physical-board gate, which remains open, and it does not turn any prediction into a measurement. The 24 GB-class windows are validated on a capped-budget, ballasted proxy on an RTX 5090. No 24 GB board has been started.

amendments.what: flip item (1) is CLOSED by measurement, and the 16 GB no-go changes its basis from arithmetic to fidelity

measurement.artifact: S16-V (full_attention K4, linear_attention K3, MLP gate/up/down K3, lm_head K4, MTP all-K4, BF16 vision)
measurement.suite: shard 0 of the v5 ladder, 512 contexts, 1,048,064 scored positions, same reference capture and shared BF16 head as every published mean
measurement.strata: all five lose with intervals excluding zero; worst code and literary, best scientific

pre_registration_outcome.rule: NO if mean > 0.030; BORDERLINE if <= 0.030; YES if <= K4's 0.010345
pre_registration_outcome.registered_point_estimate_miss: 0.0689 was 1.52x too high - the build is better than the byte-law estimate and still far short; miss published by magnitude and direction

basis_change.was: the class was published as lost on an arithmetic argument: predicted resident 13.58 GiB against budgets of 12.70 and 12.49, i.e. 0.88-1.09 GiB over before a single KV byte
basis_change.now: with the first loader term ever measured for a sub-4-bit build (+0.0402 GiB at a 12.7698 GiB payload, against the +0.35 [P] planning allowance) the int8-embedding resident figure is 11.626 GiB - 1.07 and 0.86 GiB of headroom against the same two budgets. The weights fit comfortably.
basis_change.consequence: the 16 GB no-go now rests on measured fidelity rather than on bytes, which is a harder and cleaner finding; the arithmetic paragraphs stand only as the reasoning available before the measurement existed

amendments.byte_law_check: the affine law predicted 13,711,503,428 B of payload and the conversion landed 13,711,503,428 B - zero error, its first test below 4 bits
still_open_flip_items: (3) needle and image-plus-text at the 4.2 MP cap on a K3 body
amendments.artifact_disposition: kept and published rather than deleted, because a NO nobody can audit is an assertion; it is also the empirical anchor for the K3 rung of docs/37's per-bit law
